records.wording: NA27, without its last clause, "for they perceived that he had told this parable against them". Epiphanius quotes the verse as present, but the parable of the tenants (20:9–17) is absent by his own statement (sch. 55). The clause referring to it is not quoted and is classed probably absent with the parable. In this text the verse follows the question about John's baptism (20:1–8), and the hostility it reports answers that exchange. Epiphanius' refutation introduces the verse with the setting of 20:1 ("as he was teaching in the temple").

records.wording: Marcionite reading adopted, against Roth's grade (probable): "those whom God has deemed worthy" (οὓς δὲ κατηξίωσεν ὁ θεός) for NA27 "those who are deemed worthy" (οἱ δὲ καταξιωθέντες). Tertullian quotes the clause three times with God as subject. He reports that the Marcionites read "the God of that age" together, as a second God, and he argues against that punctuation but not against the text. Their reading requires the wording, as Roth notes ("the interpretation… requires ὁ θεός to be an external subject"). Only the attested element is changed. Roth's fuller retroversion (τῆς κληρονομίας for τυχεῖν, from possessione) is not adopted; NA27's τυχεῖν is kept, so that the Greek reads "whom God has deemed worthy to attain that age and the resurrection".
